source: KSQAAC Spardha Yashassu NMMS Study Material 2022, MAT Chapter 35 (questions: PDF pages 98–99, key: PDF page 173)

questions.prompt: A clock shows 9 o'clock in the morning. Through how many degrees will the hour hand turn by the time the clock shows 3 o'clock in the afternoon?
questions.rule: The hour hand turns 30° every hour (360° in 12 hours).

questions.prompt: Find the reflex angle between the minute hand and the hour hand at 6:30 pm.
questions.rule: The minute hand moves 6° a minute. The hour hand moves 30° an hour and ½° a minute. Measure both from 12.
questions.working: Hour hand: 30 × 6 + ½ × 30 = 195°. Minute hand: 6 × 30 = 180°. They are 15° apart, so the reflex angle is 360° − 15° = 345°
questions.note: The book's key says B (315°), but the hands are only 15° apart at 6:30, so the reflex angle is 345°.

questions.prompt: If the water image of a clock shows 2:25, what is the actual time?
questions.rule: A water image turns the clock upside down.
questions.note: Hidden until checked: the English asks about a water image showing 2:25 and the Kannada about 9:25, and neither gives the key's 3:05 by the usual rule (take the image time away from 18:30).

questions.prompt: Looking in a mirror, a clock seems to show 4:45. What is the real time?
questions.rule: A mirror swaps left and right. The real time and the mirror time always add up to 12:00 (take the mirror time away from 11:60).
questions.note: Hidden until checked: the real time is 7:15, which is not an option, and the key's answer (6:25) isn't among the options either.

questions.prompt: Looking in a mirror, a clock seems to show 11:25. What is the real time?
questions.rule: A mirror swaps left and right. The real time and the mirror time always add up to 12:00 (take the mirror time away from 11:60).

questions.prompt: What is the angle between the minute hand and the hour hand at 5:50?
questions.rule: The minute hand moves 6° a minute. The hour hand moves 30° an hour and ½° a minute. Measure both from 12.

questions.prompt: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 9:10?
questions.rule: The minute hand moves 6° a minute. The hour hand moves 30° an hour and ½° a minute. Measure both from 12. "The angle between the hands" means the smaller angle.
questions.working: Hour hand: 30 × 9 + ½ × 10 = 275°. Minute hand: 6 × 10 = 60°. 275° − 60° = 215°, so the smaller angle is 360° − 215° = 145°
questions.note: 215° is the other (reflex) angle between the same hands. By convention, "the angle between the hands" means the smaller one.

questions.prompt: What is the reflex angle between the hands of a clock at 7:28?
questions.rule: The minute hand moves 6° a minute. The hour hand moves 30° an hour and ½° a minute. Measure both from 12.
questions.working: Hour hand: 30 × 7 + ½ × 28 = 224°. Minute hand: 6 × 28 = 168°. They are 56° apart, so the reflex angle is 360° − 56° = 304°

questions.prompt: A watch gains 15 minutes every day. It is set right at 12 noon. What time will it show when the real time is 4:00 am?
questions.rule: The clock goes wrong by the same amount every hour, so work out the share for the hours that have passed.
questions.working: From 12 noon to 4:00 am is 16 hours: 15 × 16 ÷ 24 = 10 minutes fast, so it shows 4:10 am

questions.prompt: At what time between 6 and 7 o'clock do the minute hand and the hour hand overlap?
questions.rule: The minute hand gains 5½ minute spaces on the hour hand every minute, so to gain g spaces it takes g × 12/11 minutes.
questions.working: At 6:00 the minute hand is 30 minute spaces behind. It catches up in 30 × 12/11 = 360/11 = 32 8/11 minutes, so 6:32 8/11

questions.prompt: At what time between 9 and 10 o'clock is the angle between the minute hand and the hour hand 0°?
questions.rule: The minute hand gains 5½ minute spaces on the hour hand every minute, so to gain g spaces it takes g × 12/11 minutes.
questions.working: At 9:00 the minute hand is 45 minute spaces behind. It catches up in 45 × 12/11 = 540/11 = 49 1/11 minutes, so 9:49 1/11
